# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 20 (Bi-Vb Pc20)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc20

**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** 20. Crying and beating oneself

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 20 (entitled *Rodana*, "Crying and beating oneself") is a disciplinary rule in the Vinaya Piṭaka of the Theravāda canon governing the conduct of Buddhist nuns [SuttaCentral]. The rule stipulates that a nun who cries and beats herself incurs an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. According to the origin narrative, the rule was laid down when a nun engaged in self-mortification by striking herself following a quarrel with other nuns [Hüsken 1997]. In the casuistic commentary, actions that do not combine both elements—such as beating oneself without weeping, or weeping without beating oneself—are reduced to an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*), while crying prompted by genuine misfortune involving family members, property, or sickness constitutes an exemption from fault [Hüsken 1997]. An English translation of the rule has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this precept is widely shared across Vinaya traditions. Parallels exist in Pali in the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (pc 20) and *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* (pc 20), in Chinese translations of the Dharmaguptaka (*pc 89*), Mahīśāsaka (*pc 132*), Sarvāstivāda (*pc 92*), Mūlasarvāstivāda (*pc 90*), and Mahāsāṅghika (*pc 88*) Vinayas, in Tibetan Mūlasarvāstivāda texts (*pc 158*), and in Sanskrit (*san-lo-bi-vb-pc88*) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus corroborates the Tibetan parallel, automatically aligning this rule with the Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005) across 16 matches [DharmaNexus]. In Pali-internal text reuse, DharmaNexus identifies 186 shared passages across 71 Pali texts, with the largest volumes of shared formulaic text found in other Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga rules, notably Saṅghādisesa 3 (1,856 characters, §1.3–1.11.1), Pācittiya 19 (1,818 characters, §1.3–2.1.6), and Pācittiya 15 (1,615 characters, §1.3–2.1.4) [DharmaNexus].
